When you talk about putting a quad rail on it, it's not bad. There's two front hand guard plates and almost all new rifles use the round ones. So just google up a two piece handguard you like, pull the old one off, put the new ones on and have fun.

Hint: use a strap wrench to pull down, then slip those wooden paint stirrers home depot gives out for free between the plate at the gas block and the handguard and pop them out with a screwdriver or whatever.

Quad rails are overrated and I find that they like to catch on absolutely everything unless you put grips on them and then they're huge. I would much prefer a modular tube system where you screw on rails where you want them.

If you insist on free floating the barrel, do it after you put a few hundred rounds through it. AR barrels tend to like being "shot in" when they brand new and whenever you mess with them. You will need to buy an armorer's wrench and vice block kit, because the free floating barrel nut is significantly different than the normal AR barrel nut. Also the handguard spring lives down there and it's almost impossible to get off without cutting it. You might luck out since your gun is new, but most of the beaters I've worked on are pretty stuck. Then you take off the gas block and in your case because your block has a rail on top, you throw it in the trash. Just kidding, ebay that shit since Hitlery is going to run and drive up prices again. GET DEM SHEKELS. Buy a new gas block and tube, smash the tube into the gas block and install the pin, then trim to length (if you bought shit-tier $1 tubes off ebay the chinese are selling made from spare brake line - you'll know it when your gas key gives up from being slammed into the tube 1000 times). THEN THE FUN BEGINS.
